archetypes.name: rebase-delegation
archetypes.rationale: The only substantial behavior change is rebase._sync_local_main delegating to git.sync_local_main; the Stalled guard now depends on git.sync_local_main returning the exact string 'refusing to update local main while checked out on main', but that string is not visible in the diff and may not match what the unchanged library function actually returns.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the refactored `rebase._sync_local_main` in `python/rebase.py` (diff lines ~2120–2167). The old implementation raised `Stalled` immediately when `branch == 'main'`; the new one delegates to `git.sync_local_main` and raises `Stalled` only when `result == 'refusing to update local 'main' while checked out on main'`. Verify whether `git.sync_local_main` in `python/git.py` can actually produce that exact string — specifically what it returns when `branch_force` fails on a checked-out branch. Also verify the non-main path: the old code returned early when `try_rev_parse('main')` was `None`; the new code falls through to `git.sync_local_main` in that case — confirm the semantics are preserved and no new `Stalled` can be raised on the non-main path. Check that `test_sync_local_main_missing_remote_on_main_stalls` in `python/test_rebase.py` (diff ~3383) correctly exercises the delegation chain through the ScriptRunner. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: cli-surface-regression
archetypes.rationale: Several error message strings changed during migration (e.g., branch_main now prints 'git-sh: unknown argument' instead of 'git-push.sh: unknown argument', create_main prints 'create-sh: not on a branch' instead of 'create-pr.sh: not on a branch'), which could silently break bash callers that grep stderr for the old script names.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit error message strings in the migrated CLI entrypoints in `python/push.py`, `python/pr.py`, `python/gh.py`, `python/git.py`, and `python/merge.py` and compare them against the deleted `*_cli.py` files visible in the diff. Focus on stderr messages that include a script/tool name prefix — e.g., `push.branch_main` now prints `'git-sh: unknown argument'` while `push_cli.branch_main` printed `'git-push.sh: unknown argument'`; `pr.create_main` prints `'create-sh: not on a branch'` while `pr_cli.create_main` printed `'create-pr.sh: not on a branch'`. For each discrepancy, check whether any bash scripts under `scripts/` or `skills/` parse the specific old string from stderr. Also check whether the existing test suite covers the changed error messages, or whether the new tests only inherited the new (potentially wrong) strings without asserting the old contract. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
